entries.title: The Baffler
entries.maker: Pentagram / Eddie Opara for The Baffler
entries.format: Editorial redesign for an ad-free quarterly literary journal with a companion website
entries.why: A strong editorial-system reference because the case page shows how one publication can feel democratic and unruly at the same time: the redesign uses an angular identity, typography-led sectioning, flexible opening spreads, and restrained color cues to keep a politically wide-ranging journal coherent without flattening its voice.
entries.implementationFormat: Print editorial redesign with a linked digital extension and multi-type family system

entries.title: Samba
entries.maker: PORTO ROCHA for editor Juliano Corbetta
entries.format: Biannual publication celebrating Brazilian queer culture through fashion, portraiture, and long-form photographic stories
entries.why: A strong editorial-system reference because it balances raw community-driven photography with a tightly controlled cover and index logic. The project shows how one magazine can feel loud, intimate, and collectible at once by pairing a shelf-grabbing wraparound identity with a mostly text-free interior rhythm.
entries.implementationFormat: Biannual photo-led magazine with wraparound identity, dual covers, and a structured index interrupting full-bleed editorial sequences

entries.title: Circular 22
entries.maker: Pentagram / Domenic Lippa with Jim Sutherland and Louise Sloper for Typographic Circle
entries.format: A compact 2024 redesign of Typographic Circle's member publication that turns a smaller half-size format into a tactile, print-first editorial object
entries.why: A strong editorial-system reference because it uses production decisions as editorial voice: the smaller format, overprinted imagery, fluorescent accents, displaced frontmatter, and speaker-specific monograms make the publication feel collectible and experimental without losing navigational structure.
entries.implementationFormat: Print publication redesign for Typographic Circle with a portable format, layered image treatment, fluorescent spot color, and experimental sequencing

entries.title: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
entries.maker: PORTO ROCHA for The Brooklyn Rail
entries.format: Guest-designed February 2021 bilingual Critics Page issue that turns manifesto-driven typography and black-and-white newsprint into the issue's editorial voice
entries.why: A strong editorial-system reference because it translates political and literary context into a compact publication grammar: manifesto-inspired cover language, black-and-white newsprint pacing, concrete-poetry titling, and intentionally unstable image placement make the issue feel urgent without losing editorial coherence.
entries.implementationFormat: Guest-designed February 2021 Critics Page issue for The Brooklyn Rail, published in Portuguese and English with manifesto-derived cover logic and black-and-white newsprint interiors

compositions.title: Angular logo used as a framing device
compositions.study: The redesigned logo is treated as an all-angle lockup that can sit in a cover corner or repeat as a pattern, giving the magazine an immediate identity hook without consuming the whole cover field.
compositions.reuse: Use a compact but forceful identity mark when each issue needs room for distinct artwork but still has to read instantly as part of the same publication family.

compositions.title: Typography as the main section organizer
compositions.study: Instead of keeping essays, opinion, poems, art, and stories in rigid blocks, the redesign lets type choices differentiate content categories across the issue, turning hierarchy into a reading guide rather than a fixed map.
compositions.reuse: Let typography carry content taxonomy when an editorial product wants more sequencing freedom than hard section dividers provide.

compositions.title: Flexible opening spreads with image-dialogue
compositions.study: The new grid abandons uniform article starts and gives openers more room for illustration, photography, and enlarged text, so each feature can establish its own pace before settling into body copy.
compositions.reuse: Relax opener templates when a publication needs each feature to earn attention through a distinct first spread instead of one repeated recipe.

compositions.title: Color-coded paper moods for literary sections
compositions.study: Short stories appear on sky-blue pages and poetry on yellow pages, giving the reader a tactile signal that the pace and spacing have changed without resorting to heavy chapter dividers.
compositions.reuse: Use restrained color fields or stock changes to cue a different reading mode when editorial sections should feel separate but still live inside one issue.

compositions.title: Vertical logo repeated across every edge
compositions.study: The logo is stacked vertically and allowed to wrap around the cover edges so the issue keeps announcing itself from the front, back, and spine rather than relying on one flat cover lockup.
compositions.reuse: Repeat one compact identity gesture around the object when a magazine needs strong shelf presence from multiple viewing angles.

compositions.title: Opposing front-and-back portraits as one statement
compositions.study: The publication uses two contrasting cover portraits of the same subject to foreground duality before the reader opens the issue, turning the object itself into an argument about identity.
compositions.reuse: Use paired covers when an editorial project benefits from presenting two emotional registers without choosing one definitive hero image.

compositions.title: Structured index interrupts the image flow
compositions.study: A strict index inspired by directory aesthetics cuts through the full-bleed photography, giving readers one moment of inventory and crediting before the issue returns to looser visual storytelling.
compositions.reuse: Insert one sharply structured directory spread when a photo-heavy issue needs a deliberate reset point and contributor map.

compositions.title: Mostly text-free photographic sequencing
compositions.study: Large uninterrupted image runs create a continuous emotional pace, with text held back so the magazine reads more like a sequence of encounters than a standard article package.
compositions.reuse: Let photography carry the pacing when the editorial goal is immersion and community portraiture rather than constant explanatory framing.

compositions.title: Smaller format used as a desirability move, not a downgrade
compositions.study: The redesign shifts the publication into a more portable half-size format, then compensates by raising print drama and material richness so the object feels more precious rather than reduced.
compositions.reuse: When editorial constraints force a smaller footprint, treat the format change as a chance to increase intimacy and collectibility instead of simply compressing the old layout.

compositions.title: Layered image spreads that feel textured and slightly unresolved
compositions.study: Project imagery is overlapped across spreads so some layers remain partially hidden, creating a dense printed texture that unifies very different contributors without flattening their work into identical frames.
compositions.reuse: Use controlled overlap and partial occlusion when an editorial feature set needs cohesion but should still preserve friction, discovery, and the sense of a physical printed surface.

compositions.title: Introduction and colophon repositioned deep into the sequence
compositions.study: The issue breaks expected magazine sequencing by moving the introduction and colophon roughly two-thirds into the publication, making the reader encounter the object more like a curated artifact than a standard linear periodical.
compositions.reuse: Relocate housekeeping content when a publication wants the opening stretch to feel immersive or intuitive before explanatory framing appears.

compositions.title: Fluorescent monograms establish contributor-level rhythm
compositions.study: Large abstract monograms give each speaker or contributor a distinct marker, acting as navigational pauses while keeping the issue's visual language loud and print-centric.
compositions.reuse: Create one bold recurring divider device when a multi-contributor publication needs section changes that can be recognized instantly without relying on repeated template pages.

compositions.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
compositions.title: Cover language lifted from the source text's formal energy
compositions.study: PORTO ROCHA explicitly cites Oswald de Andrade's 1928 Manifesto Antropofago as the reference point for the issue's cover and interior spread language, so the publication's visual tone grows out of the essay tradition it is revisiting rather than from a detached decorative style.
compositions.reuse: When a publication revisits one founding text or movement, let the reference document shape cover and spread behavior so the issue's graphics feel argued rather than merely themed.

compositions.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
compositions.title: Black-and-white newsprint sets the issue's baseline cadence
compositions.study: The interior holds to black-and-white layouts that embrace newsprint as a material condition, which keeps the issue grounded and lets typographic and spatial tension carry the drama instead of relying on added color spectacle.
compositions.reuse: Use a monochrome production limit as a pacing tool when an editorial object needs urgency, economy, and a sharper relationship between text, crop, and whitespace.

compositions.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
compositions.title: Headline settings borrow the compression and instability of concrete poetry
compositions.study: The case study says the title treatments are inspired by concrete poetry, which lets headlines behave like visual interruptions rather than neutral labels and gives the issue a more argumentative reading rhythm.
compositions.reuse: Treat display type as a formal essay device when feature titles need to alter reading speed and emotional tone before body copy begins.

compositions.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
compositions.title: Images refuse full grid obedience to keep ideological friction visible
compositions.study: PORTO ROCHA describes rule-breaking image placements that add tension to the issue, suggesting a layout system that keeps small moments of instability in play instead of resolving every spread into a calm editorial template.
compositions.reuse: Break image-placement rules in a controlled way when a cultural or political issue should feel charged and unfinished rather than perfectly institutional.

assets.notes: Pentagram customized the logotype from Graphik Bold so the flipped letterforms create a compact square core that can frame the cover or repeat as a pattern.
assets.reuse: Design a mark with multiple placement modes when a periodical needs both a stable masthead and adaptable cover behavior.

assets.notes: The page names distinct type roles for essays, opinion, poetry, stories, and identity furniture, using multiple families rather than one monolithic style.
assets.reuse: Build a publication typography map around editorial voice pairs, not just around headline/body defaults.

assets.notes: Color is applied as a light structural cue so literary content types shift mood while remaining part of the same overall journal system.
assets.reuse: Reserve color for section cadence when full-bleed graphics would overstate the transition.

assets.notes: The redesign ships with an explicit art-direction guide and uses commissioned illustration and photography more assertively across opening spreads.
assets.reuse: Pair a flexible grid with a clear art-direction brief so varied contributors still feel governed by one publication logic.

assets.notes: A robust condensed wordmark gives the issue urgency and keeps the title visible even when the object is rotated or stacked.
assets.reuse: Choose a dense display mark when a magazine needs identity force without adding extra cover furniture.

assets.notes: A saturated yellow cover field helps the issue read as loud and immediate while still leaving room for portraiture and typography.
assets.reuse: Use one uncompromising hero color when a publication needs instant shelf recognition.

assets.notes: Front and back cover portraits of the same subject create a two-sided identity device that echoes the issue's broader interest in contradiction and self-definition.
assets.reuse: Build a cover pair rather than a single hero when the subject matter benefits from tension between personas or moods.

assets.notes: The index uses a directory-like typographic voice to catalogue contributors and restore order after stretches of image-led sequencing.
assets.reuse: Borrow directory or registry cues when an editorial object needs a functional checkpoint without switching to a generic contents page.

assets.role: Tension between editorial structure and image play
assets.notes: The redesign pairs Akzidenz-Grotesk with Baskerville so the magazine can move between typographic restraint and expressive collision without losing legibility.
assets.reuse: Build editorial contrast from a deliberate serif and sans pairing when you need both institutional clarity and more eccentric visual behavior.

assets.role: Print energy and unifying highlight system
assets.notes: Fluorescent orange is used as a recurring overprint accent that sharpens overlaps, reinforces materiality, and helps the smaller format keep visual intensity.
assets.reuse: Reserve one high-energy spot color for overlays and emphasis when a printed editorial object needs a strong cross-issue signature.

assets.notes: Abstract oversized initials operate like section markers while still feeling experimental enough for a typographic society publication.
assets.reuse: Use simplified monogram sets when a publication needs a repeatable contributor marker that is bolder than a running header but lighter than a full title page.

assets.notes: The production system leans on foil and other print effects to make the reduced format feel premium and intentionally object-like.
assets.reuse: Add one tactile finishing move when an editorial redesign needs to signal desirability through craft rather than through larger page size or heavier content.

assets.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
assets.role: Typographic bridge between manifesto voice and editorial clarity
assets.notes: The issue pairs Girott's declarative letterforms with the more poetic tone of Art Company Mono, giving the publication a type system that can shift between statement, annotation, and literary pacing.
assets.reuse: Pair one forceful display family with one more idiosyncratic secondary voice when an editorial issue needs both ideological emphasis and textured reading rhythm.

assets.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
assets.notes: The declarative headline letterforms are used to echo the formal qualities and urgency of the Cannibal Manifesto without turning the issue into a facsimile.
assets.reuse: Reference a movement's typographic mood through abstraction instead of imitation when a publication wants intellectual lineage without derivative pastiche.

assets.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
assets.role: Material constraint turned into issue identity
assets.notes: Black-and-white layouts are treated as a deliberate medium choice, making contrast, crop, and spacing do the expressive work usually assigned to richer palettes.
assets.reuse: Let production constraints become the visual signature when an editorial project needs a crisp, durable system that can survive many contributors.

assets.entryTitle: Brooklyn Rail: Only Anthropophagy Unites Us?
assets.notes: Title settings influenced by concrete poetry function as recurring pressure points inside the issue, pushing the publication away from a neutral magazine voice.
assets.reuse: Build one distinct title treatment family when an editorial project needs each piece to enter with formal tension rather than with standardized feature furniture.
